newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Court rejects Sun Diamond move in Espy probe.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Court rejects Sun Diamond move in Espy probe.

text.p: A U.S. District Court rejected a motion to dismiss nine counts against Sun Diamond Growers of California arising out of the Independent Counsel probe of former Agriculture Secretary Mike Espy.
Sun Diamond goes on a trial Monday, charged with illegally trying to influence Espy while he was Agriculture Secretary with expensive gifts and favors.

In an order issued late Saturday, the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia affirmed the Independent Counsel's authority to bring the case against Sun Diamond and rejected all of the agricultural cooperative's arguments to dismiss.

The charges against the giant fruit cooperative, whose affiliates include Sun Maid raisins, Sunsweet prunes and Diamond Walnut, have arisen out of a sprawling two-year, $5 million criminal investigation of Espy being conducted by Independent Counsel Donald Smaltz.

In its motion to dismiss, Sun Diamond argued that seven of the nine counts were not related to the alleged acceptence of improper gratuities by Espy and hence were outside the scope of the Independent Counsel's jurisdiction.
The seven counts relate to an alleged illegal campaign contribution to Espy's brother Henry.

"The court concludes that the Independent Counsel has not exceeded his jurisdictional mandate because the counts in question are related to the original subject matter of the investigation," the court wrote.
